label: mid-original-phase token after an early q, in sequences starting r/g (very sparse)
explanation: Extremely sparse (19 dev steps, one per sequence, small magnitudes 0.10-0.15). It fires only in the original phase at positions 3-5 (mostly 4) and never on <DEL> or in the copy phase. Nearly every activation has the prefix pattern [r|g] ? q [c|j] x: the first token is r (about 70% of mass) or g, q is at position 1-2 (prev2_tok=q makes up 72% of mass), and the previous token is c or j. The current token tends to be o/p/k/l/2. The largest activations (o after r g q y a, p after r r q a j) fit this pattern. The context description reaches about 0.68 recall, but precision is only about 3%: the feature fires on just a few percent of steps that match the prefix, so it reads like a sharp threshold on a conjunction of prefix tokens that these variables do not fully capture. Magnitude is nearly constant and I found nothing that modulates it.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 13 cues. Raise it: orig0=r (+2.66), orig2=q (+2.23), prev_tok=c (+2.15), prev3_tok=g (+1.86), prev2_tok=q (+1.63), prev_tok=j (+1.49). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-1.92), prev3_tok=- (-1.69), in_first=0 (-1.28), n_digits=1 (-1.04).
